cf:fighter-opening-stop.wants: c.halt(on=), plus movement.walk asking whether the mover may still move between steps rather than only before the first one
cf:fighter-opening-stop.why: the card is imported now and its second sentence is a real clause -- an enemy hit by the opportunity attack stops moving, if a move provoked it -- but the window opens inside walk's loop and step never re-asks can_move, so immobilising the mover there leaves it walking the rest of its path

cf:fighter-talent-rest.wants: a hand key in the attack context (the p7399 gap), Gear recording a free/empty off hand, an armour field on chargen.Build, and improvised weapons
cf:fighter-talent-rest.why: three of the six talents are left: one turns on wielding an off-hand weapon, one on an empty off hand, and one on improvised weapons and on not wearing heavy armour -- the chassis wears scale and Build cannot say otherwise, so each would be a gate that is false for every fighter in the tree

cf:ranger-style-beast.wants: the beast companion (the p10594 gap), and then a leg in chargen.BUILDS["ranger"] for it
cf:ranger-style-beast.why: the other four styles are written or are a bonus feat; this one is a second creature on the board that also rewrites the class's extra damage, and a leg with no creature behind it would deal a ranger missing its feature

cf:rogue-melee-talent-die.wants: a thrown light blade in chargen, plus c.step_die() -- a modifier that moves a weapon's damage die one size
cf:rogue-melee-talent-die.why: the card's first sentence raises the die of a weapon no chassis carries, and nothing in the modifier language steps a die at all, so both halves of the clause are missing rather than one

cf:wizard-implement-rest.wants: legs in chargen.BUILDS["wizard"] for the three masteries with none, plus c.store_row(ref) for the one that banks an unprepared encounter power and a summon-time damage hook for the one that pays its summoned creatures
cf:wizard-implement-rest.why: the page's build sections name a class feature for two builds the tree has no leg for, and a third mastery no build names at all. Each of the three is a real clause -- bank a power, pay a summoning, repeat a missed illusion against a second target -- and none of the three has anything for c.build to answer, so adding a leg first would deal a wizard whose mastery does nothing. The docstring on cf:wizard-implement claimed this file already said so; it did not

cf:sorcerer-soul-pierce.wants: c.ignore_resistance(dtype, up_to=), read by resolve.damage before Defences.resist is subtracted
cf:sorcerer-soul-pierce.why: both written halves of the sorcerer's source end with the same clause -- the caster's arcane powers ignore a target's resistance to the sworn type up to the value of the caster's own -- and resistance is subtracted from a flat number on the target with nothing on the attacker's side consulted, so the clause has nowhere to be read

cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.wants: an event announcing a power use's finished effects (the p10354 gap), carrying the natural roll
cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.why: each source ends with a rider on a natural 20 -- and one of them a second on a natural 1 -- that lands after the attack's other effects. AttackRolled is the only event carrying the natural and it fires before the damage, so a slide-and-prone hung there would resolve in the wrong order, and Hit carries no natural at all

cf:sorcerer-soul-rest.wants: legs in chargen.BUILDS["sorcerer"] for the two sources that have none, plus a short rest for the phase one of them cycles on
cf:sorcerer-soul-rest.why: the page prints four sources and two are written; of the other two, one is a three-phase cycle clocked on a rest the engine does not have, and the other is two resistances at once with an immediate interrupt that trades them for a defence bonus. A leg for either with no feature behind it would deal a sorcerer with no class feature at all

cf:warlord-archer.why: spec.py can read the class page now and the card is three clauses: it drops two proficiencies, adds one, and lets a ranged basic attack with a bow roll Strength for the attack and the damage. basic.RANGED fixes its ability in the header and nothing can rewrite it for one creature; a bow on a warlord leg in chargen.BUILDS is wanted too, because no leg carries one and there would be nothing to shoot with

p10354.wants: an event announcing a power use's finished set of attack rolls, plus c.reroll_attack(all=True) over it
p10354.why: the earlier misses have already resolved and their bodies have already branched on them, so there is nothing left to reroll when the free action answers

p10744.wants: a thrown weapon or a sling in chargen, before c.range_bonus(mult=) is worth adding
p10744.why: every weapon in the table is a mace, bow or crossbow, so a thrown-or-sling gate would be false for every character in the tree

p11603.wants: a compendium ref for the second printed stanza
p11603.why: spec.py folds both stanzas into one entry and the compendium carries no separate id, so c.grant_row has nothing to name

p13887.wants: c.link plus link-aware query.distance_between / query.adjacent and a teleport-flavoured step
p13887.why: the card makes the two squares adjacent for movement OR melee attacks and calls the crossing teleportation; c.link as built is movement-only, so the row would silently drop the melee half

p13984.wants: a stat block for the creature it summons
p13984.why: blocked on content rather than on the engine -- the spec prints no creature, so summon=/c.summon_inline have nothing to carry

p14510.wants: a compendium ref for the other druid power its Requirement and Effect both name
p14510.why: no id in the spec and it cannot be identified from this card's mechanics; c.restore_use and c.recast both exist now

p3839.wants: a plural companion API: dsl.measured_from and dsl.roller each return one eid and must let the shaman pick which spirit an attack is measured and rolled from; c.call_companion must stop relocating when a second is allowed
p3839.why: its second and third sentences change how ~60 existing shaman rows read "your spirit companion", so it cannot be honoured by adding a method

p4396.wants: a run action in the engine -- actions._movement offering it, movement walking speed + 2, and the combat-advantage grant
p4396.why: the engine builds no run action, so neither printed clause has a subject; c.run(n) alone would not be enough

p4807.wants: Keyword.RAGE declared on the 41 rage rows (the compendium prints it in their type line), plus c.expend(ref)
p4807.why: nothing at runtime tells a rage daily from any other barbarian daily; group= is the wrong field, the engine reads it as one-per-encounter

p5591.wants: a separate compendium ref for a guardian form's attack
p5591.why: the forms (p5106, p9825, p9859) bundle their attack under the same ref, so there is no second id for c.restore_use and inventing one would be inventing an id

p5845.wants: AttackResult.parity plus c.treat_roll_as("odd"|"even"), and the two rows reading result.natural % 2 moved onto it
p5845.why: nothing can dictate what another row reads off natural, and there is no event for "you are about to use a parity power" to trigger on

p7399.wants: a hand key in the attack context, set from a header field or c.strike(hand="off")
p7399.why: c.w(hand="off") picks the dice only, so a grant gated on an off-hand attack would read a key the context does not carry

p9665.wants: Summon.instinctive on the header block, plus c.instinctive(who) and a repeatable once-per-round minor-action grant
p9665.why: no summon block in the tree carries an instinctive effect and the field does not exist, so the method would be silently false on all 40 of them -- the row would look finished and never do anything
